# a11y.aria-roles — role value is unknown, abstract, or not allowed on the element

- **Check ID:** `a11y.aria-roles`
- **Default severity:** `error`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** WCAG 4.1.2
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/a11y.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/a11y.aria-roles.md`](../a11y.aria-roles.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

A `role` value is not a WAI-ARIA role, is an abstract role, or is not allowed on that element.

## Why it matters

A `role` changes what an element is to assistive technology. A misspelled or invented role is ignored, so the element keeps its default meaning and the page does not work as the author intended: a "button" made from a `<div role="buton">` is announced as plain text. Abstract roles exist only to organize the specification. A role the element is not allowed to have, such as `role="button"` on a heading, can remove the heading from the page outline or confuse screen readers about what the element is.

## What it checks

- **Unknown role** (error): a `role` with no token that is a WAI-ARIA 1.2 role. The value is a space-separated fallback list, so `role="foo button"` is accepted, because the first role a browser knows is the one it uses. If a name is within two edits of a real role, the message says "Did you mean".
- **Abstract role** (error): `command`, `composite`, `input`, `landmark`, `range`, `roletype`, `section`, `sectionhead`, `select`, `structure`, `widget`, `window`.
- **Role not allowed on the element** (warning): for `<button>`, `<h1>`–`<h6>`, `<ul>`, `<ol>`, `<li>`, `<nav>`, and `<hr>`, the roles that [ARIA in HTML](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/) allows, plus the element's own role. Other elements are not checked, because their allowed roles depend on attributes or are nearly unrestricted.

Role names are compared without regard to case. Digital Publishing (`doc-*`) and Graphics (`graphics-*`) roles are known roles.

## How to fix

```html
<!-- before -->
<div role="buton">Save</div>
<h2 role="button">Open</h2>

<!-- after: prefer native elements -->
<button>Save</button>
<h2><button>Open</button></h2>
```

Native elements already have the right role and keyboard behavior, so no `role` is needed. There is no automatic edit, because the right replacement depends on what the element does.

None.
